title: Pine forest soy candle
subtitle: A resinous, woodsy jar candle for autumn and winter
excerpt: A soy wax jar candle scented with a pine and cedarwood fragrance oil blend, resinous, green, and dry. Well suited to living rooms and home offices in the colder months. Makes one 200 ml jar; burns for around 35 hours.
sourceNotes: Pine and cedarwood fragrance blend: woody-resinous character with a green pine top note. Fragrance load 6-7% of wax weight in soy gives a strong cold throw and moderate hot throw. Soy container candles: pour temperature 60-65°C. Pine EOs have a flash point around 50°C; for safety and scent retention use a blended fragrance oil with a higher flash point rather than pure pine EO in high concentration. Wick: CD-12 for 7 cm jar.

recipe.batchNotes: Scales cleanly. Make in autumn for the best seasonal timing, the pine-forest scent suits the colder months well.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Allow 24-48 hours cure before burning for the best cold throw.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Effectively indefinite. The resinous base note of cedarwood holds well; the volatile pine top note fades after 18 months but the cedarwood remains.

glossaryTerms.definition: The temperature at which the melted soy wax is poured into the jar. For container soy wax, 60-65°C gives a smooth surface finish and good fragrance retention.
The first burn of a candle, long enough to melt the soy wax across the full jar diameter, establishing the pool depth for every subsequent burn.

content.text: Pine forest soy candle is a resinous, woodsy jar candle with a green pine top note and a dry cedarwood base. A blended fragrance oil gives the pine character without the low flash point risk of pure pine essential oil at high concentration. Good in a living room or home office on a cold afternoon. One 200 ml jar; burns for around 35 hours.

items.prepNote: container-grade soy wax; melt point 48-53°C; pour at 55-60°C
6.9% of wax weight; add when wax is at 60°C
